name: Long-term frozen storage of 40% (wt/vol) glycerol red blood cell units at -80 C (FDA/AABB: frozen at -65 C or colder, up to 10 years)
plain_name: Store rare-type donor red cells frozen for a decade
description: Rare-phenotype RBC units cryopreserved in 40% wt/vol glycerol are kept in a mechanical freezer at -80 C for 10 years or more, then thawed and deglycerolized; the AABB/FDA circular requires freezing at -65 C or colder.
keywords: Store rare-type donor red cells frozen for a decade

sources.citation: Lecak J, Scott K, Young C, Hannon J, Acker JP. Evaluation of red blood cells stored at -80 degrees C in excess of 10 years. Transfusion 2004. DOI 10.1111/j.1537-2995.2004.03271.x
Circular of Information for the Use of Human Blood and Blood Components (AABB, American Red Cross, America's Blood Centers, Armed Services Blood Program)

requirements.rationale: The approved high-glycerol method stores the units at -80 C.
Regulatory limit: frozen RBCs are frozen and kept at -65 C or colder.
Machines documenting only a base temperature must reach -80 C.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
